GIT Surgeon
Spirit Main Hospital
Newark Road
Brisbane


19/12/2019
Re: Mr Fred Davies
Dear Doctor,
Thank you for urgently admitting Mr Fred Davies, a 65-year-old gentleman gentlman who was
admitted to our hospital with symptoms and signs suggestive of possible acute colonic pseudo -
obstruction and is being transferred transfered to your hospital for further assessment and
investigation.
Today, Mr Fred presented to our Emergency Department complaining of mild pain related to a
hugely distended abdomen and associated with lack of appetite and nausea over the past 4
days . He reported that last bowel movement was 5 days ago and denied any fever, chills or
chest pain. However, he reported difficulty in breathing.
On examination his vital signs were within normal range except for a tachycardia of 114 beats
per minute and low saturation of 92% on room air. His abdominal palpation revealed mild
diffuse tenderness with no evidence of rebound and guarding.
His laboratory findings shows leucocitosis of 14000 and his potassium postassium, BUN               Commented [PQ1]: Leucocytosis (or leukocytosis
and aspartate aminotransferase were 3.5 , 43 , and 46 respectively repectively. All other
laboratory values were unremarkable. Massive colonic dilatation that involves the cecum             Commented [PQ2]: 3.5, 43, and 46 respectively
secum, ascending colon and transverse colon was detected on imaging.
Mr Davies has a medical history of hypothyroidism, COPD, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia for
which he takes the following medications: levothyroxine, amlodipine, atrovastatin, albuterol
inhaler, budesonide, formoterole inhaler. He reported also a surgical history of meniscal tear
repair in the right knee.
It would be appreciated if you could provide Mr Davies with a surgical assessment and
abdominopelvic CT scan as you deem appropriate . Should you require further information, do
not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Dr M

Overall             This is a good effort Mostafa. Well done!
                    The Name; Address, Date, Salutation and Reference Line are perfect, well done!
Comments
                    The address is formatted correctly.

                    The word count in the body of the letter is 240 words. Aim for 180-200 in the body of the
                    text. The body of the text starts after the salutation e.g. “Dear Dr. Jones” and ends before
                    a generic closing e.g. “Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any further queries.
                    It does not include the name of the recipient and the date and the address or the sign off
                    e.g. “Yours sincerely,”


                    There are many issues with spaces. Include a space after commas and full stops.
                    INCORRECT
                    Thank you for your help in the matter.Please find test results attached.
                    CORRECT
                    Thank you for your help in the matter. Please find test results attached.
                    INCORRECT
                    The patient,who is suffering from depression,is unable to shower independently.
                    CORRECT
                    The patient, who is suffering from depression, is unable to shower independently.

                    There are some spelling issues.

                    Verb tenses are good.

                    There are some issues with punctuation, grammar and word choice.

                    Practice proofreading your writing and try to give yourself a few minutes to proofread at
                    the end of the 45 minutes in the exam.

                    Please read the sample letter and compare your letter to it.

                    Review the worksheets in the Grammar and Vocabulary Clinic.

                    Great job!

                    Grade: 360
